one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall in the window: Q2 was reported Aug 4 and Q3-25 on Nov 3, and no Q3-26 date has been filed, so results most likely land in the first week of November, after Oct 31. In-window items: (1) Black Pearl Data Hall 2 (35 IT MW) targeted rack-ready Oct 31 [8]; (2) first Barber Lake rent commencement, guided to 'the fourth quarter of 2026' [5], not specifically October, so a release may or may not fall in the window; (3) possible new HPC lease news at Odessa, Ulysses or Reveille [3], a right-tail event (the AWS lease moved the stock ~+19%); (4) the late-October FOMC and hyperscaler capex prints, with the 10-yr at 5.24% [13] weighing on long-duration AI-infrastructure names. Revised: the V3/Bitfury Oct 23 and Nov 30 tranches (1.805M shares each) settle a variable prepaid forward struck on 2025-11-03 for $100M up front [11], which the dealer hedged at inception, so they are not new supply and I drop the round-1 downward tilt for them. The unscheduled 56.5M-share V3 stake remains a background risk, not a dated event. Lognormal centred at $15.40 (a small tilt for rates only), sigma 0.30, slightly below the 112%/3.5 = 32% rule because no earnings fall in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend on 496M FD shares, valued at Oct-2027: split-rate DCF of the three signed leases (AWS at 6.5%, Fluidstack term at 7.25%, AI-lab years at 8.0%, everything else at a 9.0% WACC) with explicit renewal at expiry plus a $1.30B site-by-site probability-weighted pipeline, $7.3 (40%; single-rate $6.23); SOTP at a 6.5% cap on site-built 2028 NOI of $718M plus $/MW pipeline, $12.81 (35%); 18x 2028E EBITDA of $559M plus pipeline, $13.13 (25%); less $4.855B adjusted net debt. Blended $10.69. The price still assumes several more leases than are signed.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Round 4: site-by-site unlevered DCF valued at 2027-10-01 with split discount rates. Black Pearl (AWS, 216 IT MW, $5.5B/15y, yr-1 $296M, 3% esc, NNN 99% margin, ~2027-2042) and Stingray (AWS, 70 IT MW, $2.0B/15y, yr-1 $108M, Apr-27 to ~2042) at 6.5%; Barber Lake Fluidstack term (207 IT MW, $3.8B/10y, yr-1 $331M, modified gross 90% margin, ~2027-2037) at 7.25% plus a first-refresh default term (15% x unbacked 55% x 35% severity on rent after 2032.75, -$0.04/sh); Barber Lake AI-lab years 11-20 ($5.2B, 2037-2047, no guarantee) at 8.0% after a 10% expected-loss haircut. Post-expiry (supervisor fix): 75% renew at 85% of final rent with $1.0M/IT MW refit, 25% vacant 18 months then re-let at 85% with $2.0M/IT MW refit, +2%/yr for 10 years, then an 8.5% cap; all post-expiry, pipeline and terminal flows at the 9.0% WACC. Overhead $150M/yr +3% to 2057 then capitalized, discounted at 6.9% (contracted-weighted) during the contract years and 9.0% after; 1.5% maintenance; 21% cash tax from 2031 after ~$250M/yr depreciation. EV $7.17B (BP $4.19B incl. $1.14B post-expiry, Stingray $1.53B incl. $0.41B, Barber Lake $4.27B incl. $0.91B, overhead -$2.82B) + probability-weighted pipeline $1.30B + Odessa mining $0.01B - adjusted net debt $4.855B = $3.62B / 496M = $7.30. Single-rate (everything at 9.0%): EV $6.64B -> $6.23. Contracted-only (split) $4.69. GPU life 5/6/7 yrs: $6.76/$7.30/$7.67 split.

Amazon.com guarantees rent (AA/A1). +40bp over the note cost for duration beyond the 2031 note maturities (equity holds the 2031-42 tail and refinancing) and residual operating risk (180-day grid-outage remedy, single remote site). Stingray completion risk is small: Amazon absorbs overruns above $10.5M/IT MW [6]

inputs_detail.input: Contracted discount rate, Barber Lake Fluidstack term
inputs_detail.derivation: Fluidstack is unrated; Google backstops ~$1.73B (~45%) of ~$3.8B rent [23] (10-Q carries a $544.5M backstop asset [2]). The Cipher Compute notes secured on this lease cost 7.125% (+~190bp) [24], so the market already prices it ~100bp wider than AWS; +10-15bp for the term running to 2037 vs the 2030 notes. Supervisor correction kept: the unbacked ~55% is exposed at the first tenant fleet refresh (~2032-33): 15% default probability x 55% x 35% loss after re-leasing energized power = -$0.04/sh

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate and haircut, Barber Lake AI-lab years 11-20
inputs_detail.value: 8.0% on rent after a 10% expected-loss haircut
inputs_detail.derivation: Unnamed counterparty, no guarantee disclosed, no debt priced against it [5][24]: placed between the Fluidstack rate and WACC. The 10% haircut (round-3 GPU-life approach: GPU tenants refresh every ~5-6 yrs as rents reprice) covers expected loss; the rate premium covers the residual uncertainty, so the two do not overlap

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Contracted campuses at a 6.5% blended cap rate on site-built 2028 NOI $718M = $11.05B (AWS ~6.0%, Barber Lake ~7.25%, NOI-weighted 58/42 = 6.5%); less overhead $150M x 10 = -$1.50B; pipeline at $/gross MW: Odessa+Ulysses+Reveille 477 MW x $1.5M + Colchis 1,000 MW x 76% x $0.35M + Mikeska/McLennan 1,000 MW x $0.35M + 2.1 GW 2030+ x $0.15M = $1.65B; Odessa mining $0.01B; less adjusted net debt $4.855B = $6.35B / 496M = $12.81

inputs_detail.derivation: BP ~$302M (99% x $305M) + Stingray ~$109M + Barber Lake ~$307M (90% x $341M). Replaces the company schedule, which predates the 2026-09-25 re-phasing [5]

Data-center REITs trade at ~22-24x FFO/AFFO (~4.2-4.5% yield) [17] and ~28-30x EV/EBITDA [18]; with the 10-yr at 5.24% [13], single-tenant hyperscale leases in remote Texas warrant ~200bp more; round 4: 6.5% equals the NOI-weighted blend of ~6.0% for Amazon-guaranteed and ~7.25% for Fluidstack/AI-lab leases, mirroring the DCF rate split [24]
Same build as the DCF: $113M cash (Q2-26 cash comp + G&A, annualized) + ~$37M normalized future SBC

Discount to EQIX ~28-30x and to 20-30x platform M&A [18] because of tenant concentration (3 tenants, 1 non-IG backstopped by Google), finite lease terms and 1.3x+ leverage; similar to DLR's ~22x FFO [17] after leverage

bear.story: The AI-capex trade cools or the market sours on neocloud credit (Fluidstack, ~55% of its term rent not Google-backstopped), Barber Lake halls slip past Q1-27 or overruns exceed the $359.3M layer Cipher absorbs, no new lease is signed in 12 months and an equity raise funds the next campus. The stock re-rates to contracted value plus a little pipeline, about my DCF ($6-7.5 single to split rate), with a 5.2%+ 10-yr pressing multiples.

base.story: Black Pearl fully delivered by about Mar-27, Barber Lake rent flowing by Q2-27, Stingray rent from Apr/May-27; run-rate NOI near $700M by end-2027. One mid-size lease (Odessa, Ulysses or Reveille) is signed and the market keeps paying ~$1.5-3B above my DCF for pipeline, so the stock sits roughly flat at $14-17. GPU rental prices stay supported by power scarcity, so the GPU-life debate does not touch CIFR's contracted rent.

bull.story: Two or more new hyperscaler leases, including a first phase at a Batch-Zero GW site, the AI-infrastructure trade re-accelerates, and the stock moves toward sell-side targets ($26-32) as the market capitalises contracted NOI at a 5.5-6% cap rate and values GW-scale pipeline.

thesis_break_reason: My contracted-only value is ~$4.7/share at split rates ($3.6 single-rate) and ~$7.3 with the $1.30B probability-weighted pipeline. Around $8 the market would be paying almost nothing above that DCF, i.e. treating the unsigned pipeline as near-worthless or the signed leases as impaired. Getting there would most likely mean something fundamental: a tenant default or dispute (Fluidstack, with only ~45% Google backstop), a further Barber Lake overrun or delay, or a pipeline that cannot be leased or financed without heavy dilution. That is more than ordinary 112%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). (1) Sites: every inventory site now appears once (site_coverage). Fixes for flags on my model: Barber Lake moved from NNN/96% to modified gross at a 90% NOI margin (Nov-2025 release guided 85-90%; 90% reproduces the company NOI schedule); the stale company 2027 schedule no longer drives anything, because the DCF starts at 2027-10-01 after every hall is delivered and the Oct-26 to Sep-27 net-debt bridge is rebuilt site by site from the re-phased dates (+$0.07B vs flat); Colchis valued at 76% and the $26M NCI no longer deducted; Canaan shares from the sold WindHQ JVs credited (~$19M at $0.359/ADS); Odessa mining and Odessa HPC conversion share the same 207 MW, so mining continues only in the 60% no-conversion branch. I checked the 8-K (tenant order, timing, no AI-lab guarantee), the 10-Q (Colchis 76%, NCI $25.7M, Canaan shares, $544.5M Google backstop asset) and the Nov-2025 release (85-90% margin, $1.73B backstop): the inventory is right on all of them. Pipeline is now valued site by site at WACC, net of capex and financing ($4.0M/IT MW near-term, $3.0M GW-scale at signing) with stated probabilities: $1.30B vs $1.4B. (2) Discounting: AWS leases at 6.5% (anchored on the 6.0-6.125% notes secured on them), Fluidstack term at 7.25% (7.125% notes) plus the supervisor's first-refresh default term, AI-lab years at 8.0% after a 10% haircut, all post-expiry, pipeline and terminal at a 9.0% WACC. Supervisor's renewal correction adopted: 75% renew at 85% with refit, 25% re-let after 18 months, then an 8.5% cap; post-expiry is now ~27% of contracted value (was ~20%). Overhead is a near-certain fixed cost, so I discount it at the contracted-weighted 6.9% during contract years, which costs $0.64/sh and keeps the split-rate gain to +$1.07. DCF: single-rate $6.23, split-rate $7.30 (round 3 $7.16). SOTP and EV/EBITDA move slightly on the site-built 2028 NOI ($718M vs $727M) and lower net debt. Fair value $10.75 -> $10.69. With the contracted-only floor up ($4.34 -> $4.69) I thin the far-left tail marginally (P>=6.18 0.890 -> 0.893); median, right tail, 1-month ladder and the $8 thesis break are unchanged because the fair value barely moved. discounting.contracted_rate: 6.5% AWS (Black Pearl, Stingray); 7.25% Fluidstack term; 8.0% AI-lab years 11-20
discounting.basis: AWS rate anchored on the secured notes raised against those leases (6.125% at par, 6.000% at 99.75, Ba2/BB-, Amazon.com AA/A1 guarantor) plus ~40bp for the 2031-42 tail and operating risk. Fluidstack (unrated, ~45% Google-backstopped) anchored on the 7.125% Cipher Compute notes plus ~10-15bp for the longer term, with an explicit first-refresh default term. Unnamed AI lab (no guarantee, no debt priced) at 8.0% after a 10% expected-loss haircut, between the Fluidstack rate and WACC. Post-expiry, pipeline and terminal at a 9.0% WACC (5.24% UST; ~45% debt at ~5% after tax, ~55% equity at ~12.5%). Overhead is discounted at 6.9% during the contract years as a near-certain fixed cost (-$0.64/sh vs WACC). Sensitivities: AWS rate 6.0%/7.0% -> $7.55/$7.04; WACC 8.5%/9.5% -> split $7.68/$6.94, single $6.90/$5.59. Reconciliation: site rows sum to $22.78/sh, less overhead $5.68 and adjusted net debt $9.79 = $7.31 (DCF $7.30 after rounding).
